question.text: A body moves along a straight path covering the initial half of its total path length at a constant speed v₁. For the remaining half of the path length, it travels with a uniform speed v₂ for one-third of the duration taken for this half, and with a uniform speed v₃ for the other two-thirds of that duration. Determine the average speed of the body across the entire journey.
conditions: first half of total distance covered at constant speed v₁
for the second half distance, speed is constant at v₂ for 1/3 of the time taken
for the remaining 2/3 of the time taken for the second half, speed is constant at v₃

figure.description: A line segment AB representing the entire journey of distance 2d is split at point C into two equal lengths of distance d. Segment AC is traversed at speed v₁. Segment CB is split at point D such that the duration for CD is t/3 with speed v₂ and the duration for DB is 2t/3 with speed v₃.

solution.approach: Split the journey into the first half distance and the second half distance, find the time for each part, then divide the total distance by the total time.

steps.text: Let the total distance be 2d; the first half distance d is covered at speed v₁.
In the second half distance d, a time t splits into 1/3 of t at v₂ and 2/3 of t at v₃, and the distance covered equals d.
Solve this equation for t in terms of d, v₂ and v₃.
Add the two times and divide the total distance 2d by the total time.
Cancel d and simplify to the final expression.

common_mistakes.text: Treating v₂ and v₃ as covering equal distances instead of the stated time fractions, which changes the time split and gives a different, incorrect expression.
